lesson.title: Learn React useEffect Hook
lesson.goal: learn the React useEffect hook: run side effects on mount and on state changes, and clean them up

steps.title: Initialize project and counter component
steps.instructions: Create a Vite React app (npm create vite@latest, React template), render <MyComponent /> in src/App.jsx, and start the dev server with npm run dev. In src/MyComponent.jsx, import useState and useEffect, create count state, and add an Add button.

targets.caption: Import both useState and useEffect from react
Define addCount using an updater function

hints: Have you created the Vite project and imported MyComponent in src/App.jsx?
Make sure useState and useEffect are both listed inside the curly braces in src/MyComponent.jsx.
Use setCount(c => c + 1) inside addCount and pass onClick={addCount} to the button.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to export default MyComponent at the bottom of the file
Passing addCount() with parentheses to onClick instead of addCount
steps.code:
import React, {useState, useEffect} from "react"; function MyComponent() { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); function addCount() { setCount(c => c + 1); } return (<>

Count: {count}

); } export default MyComponent;

steps.title: Update document title every render
steps.instructions: Call useEffect near the top of MyComponent with an arrow function and no dependency array. Update document.title to `Count: ${count}` and click Add in the browser.

targets.caption: Place useEffect near the top of your component

explanations.topic: Running side code only on mount

hints: Where inside MyComponent should useEffect be placed?
Call useEffect(() => { ... }) right below the useState declaration.
Assign document.title = `Count: ${count}`; using backticks inside the callback.
common_mistakes: Using single quotes instead of backticks for the template literal
Placing useEffect inside a nested helper function instead of the component body

steps.title: Run effect only on mount
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx pass an empty array [] as the second argument to useEffect and set document.title to a fixed string such as "My Counter Program". Click Add in the browser and confirm the tab title no longer updates on re-render.

targets.caption: Add an empty dependency array as the second argument

hints: How do you tell useEffect to run only once when the component mounts?
Add a comma after the callback function and pass [] as the second argument.
Change document.title to `My Counter Program` and end with }, []);.
common_mistakes: Omitting the comma before the dependency array
Leaving out [] which causes the effect to still run on every re-render

steps.title: Trigger effect when count changes
steps.instructions: Set document.title to `Count: ${count}` and pass [count] as the dependency array. Add a subtractCount function and a Subtract button to test incrementing and decrementing.

targets.caption: Pass count inside the dependency array

explanations.topic: Running effect on mount and when value changes

hints: Which state variable should trigger document.title to update?
Put count inside the dependency array: }, [count]);.
Duplicate addCount as subtractCount using c => c - 1 and wire it to a Subtract button.
common_mistakes: Passing count without square brackets instead of [count]
Forgetting to change + 1 to - 1 in subtractCount
steps.code: useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count}`; }, [count]); function subtractCount() { setCount(c => c - 1); } <button onClick={subtractCount}>Subtract</button>

steps.title: Track multiple dependencies with color
steps.instructions:
Add color state initialized to "green", a changeColor function toggling green/red, and a Change Color button styling the

text. Add ${color} to document.title and include color in [count, color].

targets.caption: Create a second state variable for color
Add color to the dependency array

explanations.topic: Updating effect when any dependency changes

hints: Why did the tab title not update when clicking Change Color before adding color to the array?

Use setColor(c => c === "green" ? "red" : "green") inside changeColor and apply style={{color: color}} on

.
Update the dependency array to [count, color] so either state change updates document.title.
common_mistakes: Using single curly braces style={color: color} instead of double braces style={{color: color}}
Forgetting to add color to the useEffect dependency array
steps.code:
const [color, setColor] = useState("green"); useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count} ${color}`; }, [count, color]); function changeColor() { setColor(c => c === "green" ? "red" : "green"); }

Count: {count}

steps.title: Create window dimension state and display
steps.instructions: Replace the counter code in src/MyComponent.jsx with width and height states initialized to window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight. Define handleResize to update both states and render Window Width and Window Height paragraphs.

targets.caption: Initialize width and height from the window object
Create handleResize to update width and height

hints: Which browser properties hold the viewport dimensions?
Initialize states with useState(window.innerWidth) and useState(window.innerHeight).

Write handleResize to call setWidth(window.innerWidth) and setHeight(window.innerHeight), and render them in

elements.
common_mistakes: Calling handleResize before creating the resize event listener and expecting live updates
steps.code:
const [width, setWidth] = useState(window.innerWidth); const [height, setHeight] = useState(window.innerHeight); function handleResize() { setWidth(window.innerWidth); setHeight(window.innerHeight); } return (<>

Window Width: {width}px

Window Height: {height}px

);

steps.title: Register resize listener inside useEffect
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx add a useEffect with an empty dependency array [] that calls window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize) and logs "EVENT LISTENER ADDED". Open DevTools Console and resize the window to confirm registration runs only on mount.

targets.caption: Attach the resize listener inside useEffect

explanations.topic: Why adding listeners outside useEffect causes leaks
StrictMode running effect twice in development

hints: Why did placing addEventListener directly in the component body add over 1,000 listeners?
Move window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize) into useEffect(() => { ... }, []);.
Add console.log("EVENT LISTENER ADDED"); and inspect the browser console while resizing.
common_mistakes: Omitting the empty dependency array [] on the event listener useEffect
Passing handleResize() instead of the handleResize function reference
steps.code: useEffect(() => { window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize); console.log("EVENT LISTENER ADDED"); }, []);

steps.title: Clean up resize listener on unmount
steps.instructions: Return a cleanup arrow function from the resize useEffect that calls window.removeEventListener("resize", handleResize) and logs "EVENT LISTENER REMOVED". Verify in DevTools Console that StrictMode invokes the cleanup log.

targets.caption: Remove the exact listener in the returned cleanup function

explanations.topic: Returning a cleanup function from useEffect

hints: How do you tell useEffect what code to run when the component unmounts?
Return an arrow function () => { ... } at the end of the useEffect callback.
Call window.removeEventListener("resize", handleResize); and log "EVENT LISTENER REMOVED".
common_mistakes: Running removeEventListener directly inside useEffect instead of returning a function
Passing a different callback than handleResize to removeEventListener
steps.code: return () => { window.removeEventListener("resize", handleResize); console.log("EVENT LISTENER REMOVED"); }

steps.title: Add second useEffect for document title
steps.instructions: Add a second useEffect in src/MyComponent.jsx that sets document.title to `Size: ${width} x ${height}` with [width, height] as dependencies. Resize the browser window and verify the tab title updates.

targets.caption: Add a second useEffect hook for updating the document title

explanations.topic: Using multiple useEffect hooks in one component

hints: Can a React component call useEffect more than once?
Add a second useEffect(() => { ... }, [width, height]); below the resize listener effect.
Set document.title = `Size: ${width} x ${height}`; inside the second effect.
common_mistakes: Putting document.title inside the mount-only useEffect instead of adding a second useEffect
Forgetting either width or height in the [width, height] dependency array
